ui.description: Interactive 3D assembly instructions for the Safecast bGeigieZen V4.x kit.

ui.coverSub: Geiger counter kit: M5Stack CoreS3, LND 7317 sensor, Safepulse HV supply, GPS and an 18650 cell on one board.

manual.long: The step comes from the V4.x assembly manual

orient-the-pcb.title: Orient the PCB
orient-the-pcb.text: Lay the bGeigieZen V4.x printed circuit board on the bench with the top (component) side up.

place-the-header.title: Place the 2×15 header
place-the-header.text: Insert the 2×15 pin header into the J1 holes, long side up.

notes.info: The short end of the header pins must protrude from the bottom of the board.

dry-fit-the-controller.title: Dry-fit the controller
dry-fit-the-controller.text: Line up the header pins with the sockets in the M5Stack CoreS3 and press the controller flush against the top of the PCB. Take care not to bend the pins.

notes.info: Some older kits use the M5Stack Core2 v1.1. It works the same; only its back cover differs and must be removed with the small Allen key from the kit.

fasten-with-screws.title: Fasten with two screws
fasten-with-screws.text: Turn the assembly over. Insert the two M3 screws into the captive nuts in the controller and tighten them loosely. You will remove the controller again later.

solder-the-header.title: Solder the header
solder-the-header.text: Solder the header pins to the PCB. The solder should look as if it flowed up the pins and around the PCB rings (pads).

notes.info: Some of these joints end up hidden under the controller in the final assembly.

remove-the-controller.title: Remove the controller
remove-the-controller.text: Unscrew the two screws and take the controller off for the rest of the assembly.

battery-clips.title: Battery clips
battery-clips.text: Fit the two battery clips on the underside of the board, following the outline of the 18650 battery. Clench the pins slightly, like a staple, so each clip stays put and lies flat.

notes.info: The pins should protrude evenly on the top side of the board.

solder-the-clips.title: Solder the clips
solder-the-clips.text: Solder both clips from the top of the board. The solder must flow evenly over the pins and into the holes.

notes.info: The clip pins need a lot of heat. If the solder does not flow readily, use a more powerful iron or a second iron at the same temperature. A minor gap is acceptable if the rest of the pin has a continuous fillet.

protection-diode.title: Protection diode
protection-diode.text: Match the diode to the outline on the PCB: the white or silver stripe lines up with the thick line, next to the square-pad hole. Bend the leads away from the body, insert them, solder from the top and trim the excess.

notes.info: With the fuse, the diode protects against a battery inserted backwards. Bend the leads with two pairs of pliers so the body is not stressed, and wear safety glasses when clipping: cut leads can fly.

fuse-holder.title: Fuse holder
fuse-holder.text: Insert the fuse holder into the four holes marked “FUSE 2A”, flush with the board, and solder all four pins. The fuse itself is inserted later.

charger-cable.title: Charger cable
charger-cable.text: Insert the receptacle pins into the “Qi-charger” holes with the red wire closest to the board edge, and solder them. Use the wires as a handle so the receptacle sits flush.

notes.info: Observe the polarity: the red wire goes closest to the board edge.

insulate-the-clips.title: Insulate the clips (optional)
insulate-the-clips.text: Slip the pre-cut heat-shrink tubing over the sides of the battery clips, red for positive (+) and black for negative (−), leaving 1–2 mm above the metal, then shrink it with heat. Leave the end contacts bare.

notes.info: The tubing lifts the battery slightly in the clips and pushes the board up in the case. Without kit tubing, use 6 mm (¼ in) tubing cut to 18–20 mm.

safepulse-pins.title: Safepulse pins
safepulse-pins.text: Place three pins in J4 and two in J5, with the long end and its plastic carrier on the underside of the board (the battery side).

notes.info: Do not solder the Safepulse in place until the GPS wires are soldered.
notes.model: Pin length and carrier height are illustrative.

gps-wires.title: GPS wires
gps-wires.text: Insert the four prepared wires into the four middle holes of J3 and solder them. The two outer positions stay empty. The GPS module lies upside-down next to J3 for now.

notes.info: Do not peel the wax paper from the module’s adhesive pad yet. The outer two wires (positions 1 and 6) are cut short at the module and are not used. Colours follow the kit photo: at the board, black = 3.3V (not ground!), green = RX2, yellow = TX2, blue = GND. TX and RX are crossed: the board’s TX2 goes to the GPS receive pin and RX2 to its transmit pin.
notes.model: Wire routing is illustrative; the colours and the TX/RX crossing come from the kit photo.

solder-the-safepulse.title: Solder the Safepulse
solder-the-safepulse.text: Place the Safepulse on the pins, leaving only a short length protruding through the holes, and solder.

notes.info: Keep this order: the GPS and Safepulse joints are in the same area on opposite sides of the board, and fitting either module first would block the other.

mount-the-gps.title: Mount the GPS
mount-the-gps.text: Peel the wax paper off the two-sided adhesive pad and press the GPS module onto its outline on the board.

notes.info: The module attaches with a foam pad that has adhesive on both faces. It goes on after the Safepulse pins are soldered.

mount-the-controller.title: Mount the controller
mount-the-controller.text: Press the controller onto the header pins, then fasten it with the two machine screws. Tighten them, but do not overtorque.

place-the-sensor.title: Place the LND 7317 sensor
place-the-sensor.text: Set the sensor in the back cover of the case, angled so the large anode post is near the case edge, away from the Safepulse. Press the board onto the sensor’s adhesive foam pad to make a single assembly.

notes.warning: Keep the protective cover on the sensor at all times. The mica membrane is very delicate; a puncture cannot be repaired.
notes.model: The case is not modelled: the sensor is shown fixed to the underside of the board.

wire-the-anode.title: Wire the anode
wire-the-anode.text: Tin the bare end of the red anode wire, plug its socket onto the anode post and solder the other end into one of the two “Anode” holes on the Safepulse. Cover the anode post with heat-shrink tubing.

notes.info: Tinning keeps stray strands from shorting elsewhere on the board. Either Anode hole works; they are connected internally. The anode carries 500 V, so keep the post covered.
notes.model: Routing follows the kit photo; the exact shape and length vary from build to build.

wire-the-cathode.title: Wire the cathode
wire-the-cathode.text: Cover the bare cathode wire with the 5 cm (2 in) heat-shrink tubing and shrink it. Trim any excess bare wire and solder the end into the “Cathode” hole near the J4 pins.

notes.info: You may need to trim excess bare wire before soldering it to the Safepulse.
notes.model: Routing follows the kit photo; the exact shape and length vary from build to build.

preliminary-test.title: Preliminary test
preliminary-test.text: Power the controller over USB. The boot screen warns that the SD card is missing: ignore it and press Continue (top right). On the Drive screen, confirm the sensor is registering counts.

notes.info: The GPS should answer the controller even without a position fix.

checks: Drive screen shows counts from the sensor
GPS power light is on and flashes once a second

wireless-charger.title: Wireless Qi charger
wireless-charger.text: Place the coil and interface module on the underside of the rubber liner, against the bottom of the case. Solder the battery connector wires to the module’s BAT + (red) and − (black) holes, pass the connector through a hole punched in the liner and plug it into the board. Stick the coil, face up, to the bottom of the case.

notes.info: Punch the hole offset so the module stays centred. Observe the polarity.
notes.model: Coil and module shapes and positions are illustrative; the liner and case are not shown.

card-and-battery.title: Card and battery
card-and-battery.text: Insert the preconfigured microSD card into the slot at the top of the controller. Then insert the 18650 battery (not in the kit), observing the + and − polarity: a 65 mm holder takes an unprotected flat-top cell, a 69 mm holder a protected button-top cell.

notes.warning: Never short-circuit an 18650. If it gets hot, put it in a closed metal container.
notes.model: The card and its slot position are illustrative.

place-in-the-case.title: Place in the case
place-in-the-case.text: Lower the completed assembly into the Pelican 1015 Micro Case and latch the lid shut. The fit is quite tight, so the device does not rattle in the case.

notes.model: Only the back half of the case is modelled; the lid is not shown.

assembly-complete.title: Assembly complete
assembly-complete.text: Open the case and hold the power button (right side of the controller) for half a second to switch on; hold it for three seconds to shut down. The boot screen shows the device ID.
